report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is well supported for adults with presumed *cardiac* out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (especially a witnessed sudden collapse): bystander hands-only (chest-compression–only) CPR is associated with greater survival than receiving no bystander CPR.

The most directly relevant large observational study included 5,272 adult arrests of cardiac cause in Arizona. Its authors concluded that layperson compression-only CPR was associated with increased survival compared with both conventional CPR and no bystander CPR, in a setting that publicly promoted compression-only CPR. As an observational study, it cannot completely exclude differences between people who did and did not receive CPR (for example, whether the collapse was witnessed or response times), but the direction and clinical rationale are compelling.  
https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/186668

Evidence is also strengthened by randomized trials of *dispatcher instructions*: a meta-analysis found higher survival when dispatchers instructed untrained bystanders to provide continuous compression-only CPR rather than compression-plus-breathing CPR. This does not directly randomize CPR versus none—doing so would be unethical—but supports the effectiveness and practicality of immediate uninterrupted compressions.  
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2987687/

Current international resuscitation guidance emphasizes that bystander CPR more than doubles OHCA survival and gives priority to high-quality compressions and increasing bystander-CPR use; it recommends dispatcher compression-only instructions for adult arrests.  
https://ilcor.org/uploads/BLS-2025-COSTR-Full-Chapter.pdf

**Important scope:** Hands-only CPR is the default for untrained rescuers facing an adult/teen sudden collapse. Rescue breaths remain particularly important when arrest is likely from lack of oxygen—such as drowning, overdose, or many pediatric arrests—if the rescuer is trained and able. In all cases, call emergency services and use an AED promptly.
